text:
mira: Heads up — we're seeing a spike of NVIDIA Xid errors in eu-west-1 starting ~03:10 UTC. Mostly Xid 31 and a couple Xid 13. Thinking drain/replace on the worst nodes, want opinions.

jon: Can you paste the dmesg snippet and which models were running? Xid 31 often points to illegal memory access / driver faults.

mira: dmesg snippet:
```
[ 1045.223456] NVRM: Xid (31) at 0x7f8c1a2b: PID 4321 (/opt/redwood/models/chat-svc)
[ 1045.223460] NVRM: GPU 00000000:03:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```
Also ran `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` — correctable ECC errors incrementing on GPU 2 (count +14 in last 30m).

infra-bot: alert: node gpu-eu-17 marked DEGRADED -> scheduling drain.

sam: Workloads on those nodes at time of events: heavy batching from `search-emb` and `chat-svc` (batch_size=64, seq_len≈2k), using FP16 + custom kernel quant pipeline.

jon: Xid 13 historically maps to ECC/DRAM faults or timeout; 31 can be GPU page fault or driver bug; 79 sometimes thermal/firmware. We need to correlate by driver/kernel.

mira: All affected hosts are on NVIDIA driver `525.60.11`, CUDA 11.7. Control hosts (no Xids) mostly on `515.86.01`.

ops_lead: Proposal: 1) throttle batch sizes on prod routes to reduce memory pressure; 2) drain gpu-eu-17 and gpu-eu-18, reprovision one with older driver for A/B test; 3) collect nvidia-debugdump and full dmesg for vendor.

jon: Also capture `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version`, `sudo nvidia-smi dmon -s u` during repro to catch utilization spikes. Consider enabling `NVRM` level logging.

mira: I'll kick off the drains in 5m and open INC ticket INC-2026. Quick mitigation: scaled down `search-emb` batch_size from 64->32 and limited long-context routing.

sam: :thumbsup: If it reproduces on older driver, we can blame the driver bump. If not, we look at our custom kernels (quant backend).

infra-bot: analytics snapshot: 7 Xid31, 2 Xid13, 1 Xid79 across 3 nodes in last 40m. Affected fleet slice: eu-west-1 A100-p4.

mira: Plan update — RMA if ECC correctable counters keep rising after reprovision; otherwise escalate to NVIDIA with debugdump. I'll attach logs to INC-2026 and post follow-up in #incidents.

jon: One more note — Xid 31 + 'GPU fallen off the bus' usually implies transient PCIe/driver state; check kernel ring buffer for IOMMU/pcie resets too.

mira: Good call. Pasting `dmesg | grep -i pcie` next if we see more. Thanks team.
